own_solution.law: The plate produces retardance δ = 2πΔn d/λ. Projection onto the crossed analyser gives P = P0 sin²(2α) sin²(δ/2). With consistent length units, P = 6 sin²(π × 0.0092 × 1000d/589) mW, where d is in μm. The base thickness gives 5.11962 mW. Plate thinning by 3.5, 6.5 and 11 μm gives 4.28081, 3.43846 and 2.12790 mW, respectively.
assumptions: The stated thickness applies unless a sentence specifies subsequent plate polishing.
Polishing changes thickness uniformly while preserving birefringence and axis orientation.
The lens beside the plate is outside the optical path.
The earlier measurement does not qualify the independently stated present thickness.

notes: All certified answers agree with the crossed-analyser calculation. Every listed polishing depth leaves a positive plate thickness, and no conditional regime is invoked. The relations require conversion of thickness and wavelength to a common length unit and interpretation of alpha in degrees; the certified answers correctly implement both. The claimed minimal pair T8B20/TDB47 preserves 6.5 μm and changes only the polished object. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering defect in this pass because the authors explicitly identify TD658 and T4691 as numeral-free controls, rather than claiming they preserve the number and unit. T6887/TC0D0 is also explicitly not claimed to be a minimal pair. The locked pass-1 review remains unchanged.
